newsitem.title: USA: GM reaches pact with China - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM reaches pact with China - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp has reached an agreement with the Chinese government that makes the company a leading contender to win a car-making project, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Tuesday's electronic edition, the Journal said GM and China have reached a memorandum of understanding on the joint venture, which involves a factory in Guangzhou.
The major owner of the plant is the municipal government, However, France's PSA Peugeot Citroen holds a 22 percent stake and has been trying to extricate itself.

The project would likely involve an investment of several hundred million dollars, the Journal said. It would be GM's effort to cater to individual consumers in China looking to buy small, fuel-efficient and less expensive cars.
An unnamed source identified as close to GM said that final approval is pending, but that essentially "GM has been selected as the sole negotiating partner" by China.
Other companies believed to have been involved in the bidding are Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG, Daimler-Benz AG's Mercedes-Benz unit, Honda Motor Co and Hyundai Motor Co Ltd.

"We're very proud," Louis Hughes, a GM executive vice president and president of its international operations, said at a conference in Rio De Janeiro. "We've been working very hard at this for over two years."
